title: Second look at P-L4-018: agree that labels' page effect is weaker than ordinary words' (all four transliterations, finer matching), but in Takahashi's transliteration the label effect is significant at p = 0.002
statement: Replication of P-L4-018 on all public pages, in four transliterations, with an independent script. Selection as the step: pages with at least three certain label words of three or more glyphs (vs/dsl.py SEG) and at least thirty certain non-label words. Statistic: share of label words found in the page's own non-label text. Null: each section's label sets dealt among the OTHER pages of that section (derangement), 999 deals (1999 for the IT seeds). Results: ZL 46 pages, 879 labels, 0.097 against null mean 0.083 (95th pct 0.094), p = 0.026. Takahashi (IT) 45 pages, 886 labels, 0.102 against 0.082 (95th pct 0.093), p = 0.002; three further seeds at 1999 deals give p = 0.002, 0.0005, 0.003. RF 0.073 against 0.066, p = 0.149. GC 0.072 against 0.066, p = 0.189. Finer matching: labels and held-out ordinary words (the last paragraph line of each selected page with six or more paragraph lines, words of three or more glyphs) put in 8 length x 8 frequency cells (frequency in all public non-label text: 0, 1, 2-3, 4-10, 11-25, 26-60, 61-150, more), ordinary words reweighted to the labels' cell mix, cells with fewer than three ordinary words dropped (310 to 370 labels kept). Own-page over other-page-of-section ratio, labels against ordinary words: ZL 1.10 against 1.46; IT 1.16 against 1.52; RF 1.04 against 1.40; GC 1.04 against 1.47. Verdict against the step's own check: the first failure condition is not met: once matched more finely, labels' page effect is weaker than ordinary words' in every transliteration, so the step's substantive conclusion holds (label_in_page_text would not separate language from a page-local meaningless procedure). The second failure condition IS met: Takahashi's transliteration gives a label effect at p below 0.01 (0.002, stable over seeds), while ZL, RF and GC do not. So 'labels recur in their own page barely more than elsewhere' should be qualified: a small own-page label effect exists and reaches significance in one transliteration, but it is smaller than the ordinary-word effect. Limits: my selection differs slightly from the step's (879 against 886 ZL labels); the null deals only to other pages, which may explain ZL's p of 0.026 against the step's 0.079; matching keeps only a third of the labels.
check: Rerun on the public pages with the step's exact selection and null, per transliteration; report p for IT. The qualification stands if IT stays below 0.01 under the step's own deal; the substantive claim falls if any transliteration's matched label ratio exceeds its ordinary-word ratio.
